rationale: Recovery/context-validity question on hashicorp/raft: after a restart with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, does the node's in-memory configuration still reflect the committed configuration retained in its own log? Receipt 3e2dd223dd5f43409c21066a1ca43175 (exit 0) now answers the two declared comparisons completely: with the flag on, the restarted node reports latest configuration index 0 and no voter (both assertions violated, witness event index 1) although it restored commit index 11 over 12 log entries; with the flag off the same restart reports index 1 with one voter (assertion holds, evaluated event index 3). Source reading gives the mechanism: NewRaft starts with an empty configurations struct; restoreSnapshot (api.go:655-681) is the only persistent-state producer of a configuration and the startup log scan (api.go:610-613) is the only other, but it starts at max(snapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1; restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go:724-754) runs first and advances lastApplied to the persisted commit index, so committed LogConfiguration entries at or below it are skipped and processLogs never updates r.configurations (raft.go:1366-1391). The remaining open gap - a committed configuration entry newer than the on-disk snapshot - is addressed by the second experiment submitted here, which raises SnapshotThreshold so a snapshot exists, commits an AddNonvoter configuration change and then enough further entries that the change falls below the restored commit index.

investigations.hypothesis: restoreFromCommittedLogs advances lastApplied before the startup configuration scan, so committed LogConfiguration entries at or below the restored commit index are skipped and the node keeps the snapshot (or empty) configuration.
investigations.discriminator: Restart identical stores with the flag on and off and compare configuration index, server count and hasVote immediately after NewRaft returns; then repeat with a snapshot older than a committed configuration change.

investigations.question: Does a restart with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs and a large committed backlog complete, given that restoreFromCommittedLogs calls processLogs before the FSM goroutine is started?
investigations.hypothesis: processLogs pushes one message per MaxAppendEntries-sized batch into fsmMutateCh, whose capacity is 128, while runFSM is only started after NewRaft returns; a backlog requiring more than 128 batches blocks NewRaft forever.
investigations.discriminator: Commit N committed entries with no snapshot and restart: a backlog whose batch count is below the queue capacity returns promptly, while a slightly larger one never returns within a bounded wait.

knowledge.statement: At startup the in-memory configuration (r.configurations.latest/committed) is produced only by restoreSnapshot (the latest snapshot's configuration) and by the NewRaft log scan over indexes greater than max(snapshotIndex, lastApplied). With Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, restoreFromCommittedLogs sets lastApplied to the persisted commit index before that scan, so a committed LogConfiguration entry at an index <= the restored commit index is never processed and the node keeps the snapshot configuration, or an empty configuration when no snapshot exists.
knowledge.conditions: Config.RestoreCommittedLogs=true with a LogStore implementing CommitTrackingLogStore; the persisted commit index from GetCommitIndex is at least the index of the latest committed LogConfiguration entry; no snapshot covers that entry (no snapshot at all, or snapshot.ConfigurationIndex below it).

gaps.question: Does the same loss of configuration occur when a snapshot exists whose configuration index is below the index of a committed LogConfiguration entry (entries in (snapshotIndex, restored commitIndex])?

interpretations.rationale: Receipt 75c355f2a4634b5193fa97e4de987fe0 (exit 0, six events, no parse loss) both repeats the first scenario and settles the registered gap. Its events 0-3 repeat the no-snapshot pair with the same values as receipt 3e2dd223dd5f43409c21066a1ca43175: mode on yields after_latest_index 0, after_servers 0 and after_has_vote false while after_commit_index 11 and after_last_applied 11 were restored, and the mode off control yields index 1 with one voter. Events 4 and 5 cover the snapshot-present case: before shutdown the log's latest configuration is index 1227 with two servers while the snapshot sits at index 1220 with configuration index 1 (one server), and after the restart the node reports after_latest_index 1, after_servers 1 and matches_committed_log false, so both declared comparisons are violated by witness event index 5 with admission event index 4. The mechanism is the one the source predicts: NewRaft starts with an empty configurations struct, restoreSnapshot (api.go:655-681) is the only persistent-state producer of a configuration, and the startup log scan (api.go:610-613) is the only other producer but begins at max(snapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1 because restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go:724-754) has already advanced lastApplied to the persisted commit index; processLogs forwards LogConfiguration entries to the FSM without ever updating r.configurations (raft.go:1366-1391). The node therefore resumes with a membership view that its own committed log contradicts: in the witnessed case it drops a committed membership change (an added nonvoter) that postdates its snapshot, and in the no-snapshot case it resumes with no peers at all, which runFollower's 'no known peers, aborting election' branch (raft.go:228-232) and the hasVote gate (raft.go:236-246) turn into a permanent inability to campaign, with quorumSize() (raft.go:1087-1094) computed over the stale configuration. Receipt 99b89f1a9b634301a58130e5494d394f is retained for its raw events only, since its comparisons could not correlate and returned unknown.

knowledge.assertion: Startup configuration comes only from restoreSnapshot and from the log scan above max(snapshotIndex, lastApplied), so RestoreCommittedLogs hides committed configuration entries at or below the restored commit index.

counterevidence: The control case with RestoreCommittedLogs off keeps the committed configuration in both scenarios, isolating the recovery path rather than the restart, the stores or the applied entries.
The snapshot path does supply a configuration (api.go:677-678), which is why the snapshot-present case needed a configuration change newer than the snapshot to expose the loss.
limitations: Both witnessed cases use a single voter, so consequences that require a multi-voter election (for example a node campaigning under a stale membership) are argued from the code and not witnessed.
The nonvoter addition keeps the quorum at one voter; a voter-adding change that a stale configuration would miscount is not witnessed.
The separate startup-blocking suspicion is recorded as its own question and is not part of this account.

ef5ddbf78bd4456ea51537bd60a61a80-gap-0.explanation: Resolved by receipt 75c355f2a4634b5193fa97e4de987fe0: with a snapshot at index 1220 whose configuration index is 1, a committed AddNonvoter change at index 1227 followed by further entries left the restarted node at configuration index 1 with one server instead of two (witness event index 5, admission event index 4). The loss therefore also occurs when a snapshot exists but predates the committed configuration change.

interpretations.joint_history: Receipts 3e2dd223dd5f43409c21066a1ca43175 and 75c355f2a4634b5193fa97e4de987fe0 executed the same fixed harness file and inputs for the no-snapshot pair (single bootstrapped voter, CommitTrackingLogs, ten applied entries, restart from identical stores) and emitted matching values: on gave 0/0/false and off gave 1/1/true in both. Receipt 75c355f2 additionally ran a third scenario in the same file; each receipt is a complete execution of its own scenarios rather than a fragment of the other, and the differing comparison declarations across the earlier receipts are recorded as revisions, not merged.

interpretations.rationale: Source: NewRaft's FSM queue is created with capacity 128 (api.go:558-561) and the FSM, main and snapshot goroutines are only started after the startup work at api.go:632-639; restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go:724-754) calls processLogs, which pushes one message per batch of MaxAppendEntries entries into that queue (raft.go:1296-1320). A committed backlog needing more than 128 batches therefore has no consumer while NewRaft runs. A native construction probe with the default MaxAppendEntries of 64 measured a sharp boundary: 8002 committed entries (126 batches) returned from NewRaft in 3 ms, while 8402 entries (132 batches) had not returned after a bounded 15 second wait. That probe is construction feedback without a retained receipt, so the submitted experiment repeats both sizes under controller execution and only its receipt can make this a completed comparison.
counterevidence: A backlog that stays at or below the queue capacity returns promptly, so the failure is not general slowness of log replay.
limitations: No receipt yet; the account rests on source reading plus a native probe.
The interval is a bounded wait, not an infinite-run proof; a later repair or a substantially different schedule is not excluded.
The queue capacity is taken from the source constant, not measured.

scope.description: Boot one node with RestoreCommittedLogs on and a CommitTrackingLogStore, commit 8000 and then (separately) 8400 entries without any snapshot, restart from the same stores, and report whether NewRaft returns within a bounded 15 second wait.
assumptions: MaxAppendEntries keeps its default of 64, so 8002 committed entries need 126 batches while 8402 need 132.
No snapshot is taken, so restoreFromCommittedLogs replays the whole committed log.
The two sizes bracket the FSM queue capacity without changing any production logic.
excluded: Any judgment about how long a very large but sub-capacity replay may legitimately take.
The configuration-loss finding, which is recorded under the parent question.

experiment.prefix: The harness uses the package's own test facilities (inmemConfig, MakeClusterOpts with CommitTrackingLogs, MakeClusterCustom), commits the entries through Apply, shuts the node down, and then calls NewRaft on a separate goroutine so the test itself can report a bounded wait. It emits a startup_before_restart event carrying the committed entries and indexes, then a restart_with_backlog event carrying newraft_returned together with the same operands; no production logic is modified.
experiment.responsibility: The library owns startup: NewRaft must either return or fail, and it must not depend on a component it starts after returning to make progress.

comparisons.description: With a committed backlog whose batch count exceeds the FSM queue capacity, NewRaft is expected to return (startup completes); the defect prediction is that it never returns.
Control: with a backlog whose batch count stays below the queue capacity, NewRaft is expected to return promptly, distinguishing the queue-capacity mechanism from a generally slow replay.
